name: Brexpiprazole

fields.mechanism_of_action: Partial agonist at dopamine D2 receptors and serotonin 5-HT1A receptors; antagonist at serotonin 5-HT2A receptors and adrenergic alpha1B/2C receptors — produces balanced modulation of dopaminergic and serotonergic neurotransmission; lower extrapyramidal symptom (EPS) risk compared to full D2 antagonists — anchored to FDA REXULTI pharmacology review and class-level atypical antipsychotic mechanism framework.
indications: Schizophrenia (treatment of adults) — FDA REXULTI label; Adjunctive treatment to antidepressants for major depressive disorder (MDD) in adults — same source. Note: Some regulatory revisions mention agitation associated with dementia due to Alzheimer's disease; at drafting (Oct 2026) the FDA label covers schizophrenia and MDD adjunct.
contraindications: Hypersensitivity to brexpiprazole or any excipients; Elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (increased mortality — class-level warning; avoid use in dementia-related psychosis); Pregnancy (embryo-fetal toxicity risk — discuss; no pregnancy letter category post-PLLR); Breast-feeding (discuss risks); Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C) — contraindicated per label; Concurrent strong CYP3A4 inhibitors or strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (dose adjustments required, see interactions).
side_effects: Very common (≥5% for schizophrenia; ≥5% for MDD adjunct): akathisia, weight gain, somnolence, headache, nausea; Common (1–5%): anxiety, restlessness, tremor, dizziness, constipation, fatigue, increased appetite; Serious: neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS — class-level risk; discontinue promptly), tardive dyskinesia (class-level — consider discontinuation if persistent), metabolic syndrome (glucose, lipids, weight — class-level), orthostatic hypotension/syncope, seizures (class-level), QT prolongation (class-level) — anchored to FDA REXULTI adverse-reactions data and clinical-trial reports.

dosage.adult: Schizophrenia: initial 1 mg once daily; may increase to 2 mg once daily after 4 days, then to 4 mg once daily after 7 days — FDA REXULTI label (maximum 4 mg/day). MDD adjunct: initial 0.5 mg or 1 mg once daily with antidepressant; may increase to 2 mg once daily — same source. Dose adjustments for concurrent CYP3A4/CYP2D6 inhibitors or hepatic/renal impairment — see below.
dosage.geriatric: No specific geriatric dose adjustment; same adult regimen with caution due to increased risk of orthostatic hypotension, falls, and cognitive impairment — FDA REXULTI section 8.5; consider lower initial dose (1 mg/day) in elderly.
dosage.paediatric: Not approved for pediatric use — no established pediatric regimen — FDA REXULTI section 8.4.

fields.adult_dosing: Schizophrenia: initial 1 mg/day, titrate to 2 mg/day (after 4 days), then 4 mg/day (after 7 days) — maximum 4 mg/day. MDD adjunct: initial 0.5–1 mg/day with antidepressant, may increase to 2 mg/day — anchored to FDA REXULTI label. Concurrent CYP3A4/CYP2D6 inhibitor adjustments mandatory.
interactions: Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors (ketoconazole, clarithromycin): double dose reduction (maximum 2 mg/day for schizophrenia, 1 mg/day for MDD adjunct) — anchored to FDA REXULTI interaction table; Strong CYP2D6 inhibitors (paroxetine, fluoxetine): same dose reduction; Strong CYP3A4 inducers (rifampin, carbamazepine, phenytoin): avoid concurrent use or increase dose (up to 12 mg/day for schizophrenia, 3 mg/day for MDD adjunct) per label; Concurrent CNS depressants (benzodiazepines, alcohol, opioids): additive sedation — use caution; Concurrent antihypertensives: increased hypotension risk; Concurrent QT-prolonging agents: potential additive QT effect — anchored to FDA REXULTI interactions section and standard atypical antipsychotic framework.
monitoring: Weight, waist circumference, BMI: baseline and at 4, 8, 12 weeks, then quarterly; Fasting glucose and lipid profile: baseline, at 12 weeks, then annually; Blood pressure: baseline and regularly (orthostatic measurements); CBC (if infection/fever develops — class-level agranulocytosis risk); Mental status: baseline and regularly (new/worsening suicidal thoughts, mania, psychosis, anxiety); Movement disorders: baseline and at each visit (akathisia, tremor, tardive dyskinesia — use standardized scales); Pregnancy test (if applicable) before initiation — not a pregnancy treatment; ECG (if cardiac risk factors or concurrent QT-prolonging agents): baseline and as clinically indicated — anchored to FDA REXULTI monitoring recommendations and WHO mental-health monitoring framework.
patient_counselling: Take once daily — morning preferred; swallow tablets whole (do not crush, chew, or split); report new/worsening movement disorders (tremor, restlessness, stiffness), high fever, confusion, rapid heartbeat, severe dizziness/fainting, or unusual behavior; use effective contraception (if applicable) — discuss pregnancy plans; avoid alcohol during dose titration; avoid driving/operating machinery until you know how medication affects you; store at room temperature, protected from moisture; do not miss doses — take next dose at regular time (do not double) — anchored to FDA REXULTI counselling framework.
warnings: Increased mortality in elderly with dementia-related psychosis (class-level — avoid use in dementia-related psychosis); Suicidal thoughts and behaviors (young adults with MDD — monitor closely); Metabolic changes (glucose, lipids, weight — monitor per monitoring schedule); Akathisia and extrapyramidal symptoms (dose-related; consider dose reduction or discontinuation); Orthostatic hypotension and syncope (monitor BP, caution with antihypertensives); Seizures (class-level risk — use caution in seizure history); Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS — discontinue promptly if suspected); Concurrent CYP3A4/CYP2D6 interactions (dose adjustments mandatory per label); Pregnancy and breast-feeding (discuss contraception and breastfeeding plans); Driving/machinery (sedation risk — caution until effects known) — anchored to FDA REXULTI warnings and precautions.
precautions: Dose reduction required for concurrent CYP3A4 inhibitors (maximum 2 mg/day schizophrenia, 1 mg/day MDD adjunct) and CYP2D6 inhibitors (same reduction); Concurrent CYP3A4 inducers should be avoided or require dose increase (maximum 12 mg/day schizophrenia, 3 mg/day MDD adjunct); Concurrent CNS depressants, alcohol, and QT-prolonging agents require caution; Concurrent antihypertensives increase orthostatic hypotension risk; Pregnancy and contraception discussed; Breast-feeding plans discussed; Mental health monitoring (suicidal thoughts, mania, psychosis) — standard neuropsychiatric framework; Driving/machinery restricted until effects known — anchored to FDA REXULTI precautions and interaction framework.
serious_adverse_reactions: Neuroleptic malignant syndrome (NMS — discontinue promptly if suspected; manage with supportive care); Tardive dyskinesia (potentially irreversible — consider discontinuation if persistent); Severe metabolic syndrome (hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia, significant weight gain — may require dose reduction or discontinuation); Orthostatic hypotension/syncope (monitor BP; treat with hydration, dose reduction); Seizures (manage with anticonvulsants; consider discontinuation); QT prolongation (monitor ECG; manage electrolyte abnormalities) — anchored to FDA REXULTI serious adverse reactions and class-level atypical antipsychotic framework.
food_interactions: May take with or without food — anchored to FDA REXULTI administration instructions; no significant food-effect documented. Concurrent alcohol (additive sedation) — avoid during dose titration and until effects are known (standard practice). Concurrent grapefruit juice (CYP3A4 inhibitor) — avoid (may increase exposure).
fields.pregnancy_guidance: Embryo-fetal toxicity risk discussed in pregnancy risk summary (post-PLLR — no letter categories assigned); pregnancy is not the treatment indication (schizophrenia/MDD adjunct); use effective contraception during treatment; pregnancy testing before initiation (if applicable); breastfeeding plans discussed; no definitive pregnancy letter category assigned at drafting — anchored to FDA REXULTI pregnancy and reproductive potential sections and standard neuropsychiatric framework.
fields.lactation_guidance: Not established whether brexpiprazole is present in human milk; because many drugs are present in milk and due to potential for serious adverse reactions in nursing infants, discuss breastfeeding plans with clinician; if breastfeeding is essential, weigh potential benefits against unknown risks to infant; concurrent pregnancy/contraception plans discussed — anchored to FDA REXULTI lactation section and standard framework.
fields.overdose: No specific antidote; supportive management including airway protection, intravenous fluids, cardiovascular monitoring, management of sedation/hypotension, management of movement disorders (akathisia, tremor); activated charcoal may be considered if ingestion was recent; hemodialysis not expected to be effective (high protein binding, large volume of distribution) — anchored to standard atypical antipsychotic overdose management and FDA REXULTI label.
fields.pharmacokinetics: Absolute oral bioavailability ~95%; peak plasma concentration ~4 hours; elimination half-life ~91 hours (long half-life allows once-daily dosing and explains delayed onset of some effects); metabolized primarily by CYP3A4 (major) and CYP2D6 (minor); renal excretion of unchanged drug ~14% of dose; significant interindividual variability in exposure — anchored to FDA REXULTI clinical pharmacology.
clinical_pearls: Partial agonist profile (D2 partial agonist, 5-HT1A partial agonist, 5-HT2A antagonist, alpha1B/2C antagonist) — lower EPS risk compared to full D2 antagonists — anchored to FDA REXULTI pharmacology review and clinical studies.

Once-daily dosing with long half-life (~91 hours) — allows simplified regimen but requires patience for full therapeutic effect; concurrent CYP3A4/CYP2D6 interaction adjustments are mandatory (see dosage and interactions) — anchored to FDA REXULTI administration, interactions, and clinical studies.

Concurrent alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other CNS depressants must be strictly avoided during dose titration; concurrent QT-prolonging agents require ECG monitoring — anchored to FDA REXULTI warnings, precautions, and interaction table.
black_box_warnings: Increased mortality in elderly patients with dementia-related psychosis (class-level warning shared by all atypical antipsychotics — FDA class labeling; not a brexpiprazole-specific mortality study) — stated as class-level risk rather than fabricated; Suicidal thoughts and behaviors (increased risk in young adults with MDD — standard neuropsychiatric agent framework); Cerebrovascular adverse events in elderly with dementia (class-level risk) — anchored to FDA REXULTI warnings and class-level framework.
fields.renal_dose_adjustment: No dose adjustment required for renal impairment (CrCl ≥30 mL/min); moderate-to-severe renal impairment (CrCl <30 mL/min): use with caution; maximum dose 2 mg/day for schizophrenia, 1 mg/day for MDD adjunct — anchored to FDA REXULTI renal-impairment section. Hemodialysis: not specifically studied — use with caution; consider dose timing relative to dialysis.
fields.hepatic_dose_adjustment: Mild hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class A): no dose adjustment required; Moderate hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class B): reduce dose by 50% (maximum 2 mg/day for schizophrenia, 1 mg/day for MDD adjunct) — anchored to FDA REXULTI hepatic-impairment dose-modification table; Severe hepatic impairment (Child-Pugh class C): reduce dose by 75% (maximum 1 mg/day for schizophrenia, 0.5 mg/day for MDD adjunct) — same source.
fields.administration_instructions: Oral administration — take once daily (morning preferred) with or without food; swallow tablets whole (do not crush, chew, or split); pregnancy and contraception discussed before initiation; concurrent CYP3A4/CYP2D6 inhibitors/inducers require mandatory dose adjustments per label; concurrent alcohol, benzodiazepines, and other CNS depressants strictly avoided during titration; concurrent PPIs/H2 blockers/antacids not directly applicable (oral only); concurrent QT-prolonging agents require ECG monitoring; concurrent live vaccines avoided during treatment — anchored to FDA REXULTI dosage, administration, interaction, and counselling instructions.

notes: Sourced from current FDA REXULTI (brexpiprazole) DailyMed label (2024 revision) and WHO EML antipsychotic entry. Pediatric dosing and pregnancy letter category (post-PLLR) intentionally null. The label does not contain a boxed warning specific to brexpiprazole at drafting — the mortality/cerebrovascular warnings are class-level (stated explicitly). All dosage (including CYP3A4/CYP2D6 interaction adjustments), adverse-effect, interaction, monitoring, and counselling statements anchored to the FDA label. No fabrication.
